title: Best Duvets UK
short: Wool, feather and down, and synthetic duvets compared by tog rating, breathability and season.
intro: The right duvet depends on more than tog rating alone. This guide compares duvets Ideal Home's Sleep Editor says the team tested over 10,000 hours across more than 30 bestsellers, covering winter, summer and all-season options across wool, feather and down, and synthetic fills.

guide.q: What tog rating do I need?
guide.a: As a rough guide: 1-4.5 tog suits hot summer nights, 7.5-10.5 tog suits spring and autumn, and 13.5 tog suits a cosy winter room. An all-season duvet combines two lighter duvets you can use separately or fastened together for winter.

guide.q: Wool, feather and down, or synthetic?
guide.a: Wool offers the best breathability and temperature regulation, and works well if you share a bed with someone who sleeps at a different temperature. Feather and down gives the most luxurious, squashy feel but can run warmer for hot sleepers. Synthetic microfibre is the most affordable and easiest to wash, at the cost of breathability.

guide.q: Can I machine wash my duvet?
guide.a: It depends on the fill. Synthetic duvets are generally the easiest to machine wash and tumble dry. Some wool duvets, like the Woolroom range here, are machine-washable but need line drying. Others, along with some premium wool and down duvets, are not machine washable at all, so always check the care label.

guide.q: What does a sleep trial mean?
guide.a: Some duvet brands let you sleep on the duvet at home for a set number of nights (commonly 30-60) and return it for a refund if it doesn't suit you. It's a useful way to test an expensive duvet risk-free before committing.
